description: Agent Support Operations: submit backlog and aging records with the ticket list they answer to: the backlog with its reference, the moment it is read at, the open total it states, the oldest a ticket may age untouched in days and each aging bucket with its id, band, youngest and oldest age in whole days and the tickets it places in the band; each ticket with its id, reference, the moment opened, its status, the moment last worked, the moment closed and whether a response went to the customer with the close. The signed report gives the backlog and the tickets, the stated total against the open and pending tickets in the list, each open ticket aging past the limit against a touch recorded within it, the aged tickets closed together within an hour against a response sent with the close, and the aging buckets in order against the bands they cover, and counts them, and names divergent backlog records: a backlog total that does not recompute from the ticket list, a ticket aging past the stated limit with no touch recorded, old tickets closed in bulk with no response to clear the aging, three or more aged tickets within one hour, and aging buckets that skip a band; then a bucket that overlaps the one before it and a bucket count unlike the ticket ages in the list, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No tickets, no stated total, no age limit, no buckets, or no reading moment beside open tickets leaves those points unverified. Open and pending tickets make the backlog, ages count in whole days from opening to the reading, bands run in whole days and a band with no oldest age runs on. This reads whether the backlog and its aging hold together with the ticket list beneath them. Verdict support_backlog_divergent, support_backlog_partial, support_backlog_unverified or support_backlog_consistent. POST /api/support-backlog-check. Reads the support records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it answers no customer, sends no message and opens, closes or changes no ticket, which stay with the support team, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Support Operations reads support operation records: ticket logs, first response records, resolution records, escalation records, promise records, performance records, backlog records and the support summary, each against the queue record, the stated response commitments, the customer confirmations, the stated escalation triggers, what the records show happened, the stated service commitments, the ticket list or the records beneath it. The family’s ground is support work already done, read across the whole queue: the DiligenceOps support brief reads one support conversation and lists the promises made in it, and the Agent Feedback family reads the loop around feedback on work, while this family checks whether the support operation’s records hold together across tickets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-support-operations-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-support-operations/.

age_limit_days.description: The oldest a ticket may age untouched, in days.

as_of.description: The moment the backlog is read at, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

band.description: The aging band, such as 0-2 days.

count.description: The tickets the record places in the band.

from_days.description: The youngest age in the band, in whole days.

to_days.description: The oldest age in the band, in whole days; left out for the last band.

stated_total.description: The open backlog total the record states.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

tickets.description: Each support ticket in the backlog.

closed_at.description: When the ticket was closed, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

closing_response.description: Whether a response went to the customer with the close.

last_touch_at.description: When the ticket was last worked, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

opened_at.description: When the ticket was opened, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

status.description: The ticket status: open, pending, solved or closed.

name: wever_support-backlog-check
title: Support backlog check
